newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interim chamber may spell chaos - lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: HK interim chamber may spell chaos - lawmaker.

text.p: A prominent lawmaker on Sunday warned that the operation of a Beijing-endorsed interim legislature in Hong Kong before the British colony's handover to China could spell political chaos.

The interim body is to be chosen on Saturday to replace the current chamber when Britain returns Hong Kong to China next July 1. Its formation is favoured by post-handover leader-elect Tung Chee-hwa but opposed by the Governor and democrats.

"In the unlikely event that Mr Tung can pursuade Governor Chris Patten to allow civil servants to assist the provisional legislature, he must recognise that having two legislatures operating side by side is a recipe for confusion and chaos," pro-democracy legislator Emily Lau said in a radio programme.

"If the two bodies express different views on how things should be done, the civil servants would not know what to do. The bureaucracy could be ground to a halt and the repercussions would be felt throughout the community," she said.
"Hong Kong's image as an efficient international city would go down the drain," she added.
The interim legislature, to be picked by a China-supervised college of Hong Kong luminaries, will supplant the Legislative Council elected in 1995 under Governor Chris Patten's political reforms.
China, offended by the reforms, decided to replace the current council upon the handover with a provisional body formed under the country's own supervision.
The idea of the provisional chamber does not please local democrats and its establishment before the sovereignty transfer has aroused further controversy.
